flags.estimate: Ship the datamine unchanged: reloadFrames 141, chargeFrames 60, ammo 6, hitsPerShot 2, class-default RL rate, engine 22f bolt-recovery ON (noBoltRecovery NOT set).
flags.reasoning: Datamined rate_of_fire / reloadFrames are the known-unreliable fields (prior 1). Whether an RL autofires (no bolt gap) vs takes the ~22f bolt-recovery gap is a ~15-20% shot-count swing and is NOT derivable from kit text (Liberalio root case). RL rates quantize exactly on 60fps boundaries so frame-quantization is not a concern here, but the shot-gap is. No text tell (no 'Magnum'/revolver/per-N-round flavor); 6-round magazine at ~1s charge each does not empty in <1s, so no escalation to probably-wrong.
flags.recipe: Two frames 0.5s apart on the ammo counter during an uninterrupted firing window, repeated in a second range band, gives pulls/s outright. Time reload start->refill for reloadFrames. To settle bolt recovery: measure shot-to-shot spacing at full charge; if spacing == chargeFrames with no dead gap, set charFixes.noBoltRecovery:true.

flags.estimate: Keep the datamined 2 hits per shot at normalAttackMultiplier 61.3 each (split).
flags.reasoning: Kit-silent, always-⚑ (prior 5). Cinderella's twin rockets split into two instances; Maiden's twins merge into one. The choice is a 2x swing on normal-attack damage attribution and cannot be read from prose.
flags.recipe: Record a solo full-charge sequence and count damage popups per trigger pull — two popups per shot = split (keep hitsPerShot 2), one popup at ~2x value = merge (hitsPerShot 1 with doubled multiplier).

flags.reasoning: The kit line is a stat CLAMP ('fixed at 0.7 sec'), not a percentage buff. The schema has no clamp primitive, so it is expressed as the equivalent percentage against the BASE charge time. This is exact when no other charge-speed buff is live and WRONG (under-clamps, i.e. runs cold on shot count) when a teammate also grants charge speed — the real value stays pinned at 0.7s regardless. Also assumes chargeFrames 60 is the true base (itself a datamine field).
flags.recipe: In a solo run, count full-charge shots fired in the 10s burst window: 0.7s charge + bolt recovery should give a fixed count. Then re-run with a charge-speed teammate — if the count does NOT increase, the clamp is real and the engine needs a clamp primitive (engine-modeling-gaps stat-clamp class, asuka-wille precedent).

flags.reasoning: 'Re-enters Burst and changes to Stage 1' is ambiguous prose with no exact schema primitive. Two readings: (a) she gains/retains stage-1 burst eligibility so she can be selected again on a later rotation (modeled), or (b) she immediately re-enters the burst queue WITHIN the same rotation, effectively casting twice. Reading (b) would roughly double her burst-slot contribution in a hasB1 team. She is natively Burst I, so (a) is close to a no-op — which is itself a reason to suspect (b) is the real mechanic. HYPOTHESIS, not a fact.
flags.recipe: Run a comp with another Burst I ally (the control comp's liter qualifies) and dump the burstCast events via cfg.onEvent — count anis-star casts per rotation. Two casts in one rotation confirms reading (b); one cast per rotation confirms (a).

flags.field: skill2[2].target — 'self and all allies with lower final DEF than self'
flags.reasoning: No DEF-ranked TargetDef exists in the schema. She is a Defender, so on a standard 1-defender team she is the highest-DEF unit and the approximation is exact. It OVER-credits on any team carrying a higher-DEF ally (a second Defender, or a DEF-buffed unit — note her own burst grants self DEF +55.01%, which makes her even more likely to be top). 'final DEF' implies a LIVE comparison, so a teammate's DEF buff could flip membership mid-window.
flags.recipe: Compare each ally's final DEF at FB entry in the graded comps; if any ally out-DEFs her, either add an alliesLowestDef-style TargetDef or narrow the target set by hand for that comp.

flags.estimate: crit NOT set (default DoT crit-OFF), atkPct 40.01 x 40 ticks.
flags.reasoning: Priors: DoT crit is opt-in ONLY where measured (jill's acid tick video-confirmed 99.7% non-crit; mihara's Ensnaring validated non-crit; isabel is the lone measured crit carrier). But this line reads as discrete ATTACKS ('stars ... attack random targets') on a 0.25s interval rather than a damage-over-time aura, which is the profile of a critting rider. Following the measured-over-plausible rule and leaving it off; this runs COLD if the stars do crit.
flags.recipe: Record a solo burst window and read popup colours during the 10s star barrage — orange bodies (+ crit icon) at roughly the sheet crit rate means set crit:true. 40 ticks in one window gives ample sample size.

flags.estimate: {kind:'chargeCounter', count:1} — fires on every full charge.
flags.reasoning: The kit says 'when LANDING a Full Charge attack' (rider) and 'when PERFORMING a Full Charge attack' (heal). chargeCounter advances per full charge fired, not per hit landed, so the rider's 'landing' condition is modeled as always-satisfied. Against the v1 single partless boss every full charge lands, so this is exact here; it would over-fire against a dodging/multi-target boss. Also note the wording difference between the two lines is preserved only incidentally.
flags.recipe: Confirm chargeCounter count:1 fires once per full-charge shot (not once per hitsPerShot projectile) by counting flatDamage events with bucket-tagged 120.13% against the shot count in an onEvent dump — a 2x mismatch means the counter is per-hit and needs count:2.

flags.estimate: Not modeled (only the fullBurstEnd instance ships).
flags.reasoning: The line activates 'at the start of battle AND when Full Burst ends'. At t=0 all allies' burst cooldowns are already 0, so a 7.48s reduction has nothing to reduce. Modeling it as a second passive burstCdr block risks the engine applying it as a negative offset (an effective head start) and double-counting. Deliberately omitted as inert, not dropped.
flags.recipe: Dump burstCast timestamps for rotation 1 with and without a passive oncePerBattle burstCdr block; if the first burst lands earlier with it, the game's battle-start application is real and must be modeled.
